solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A lanky Scot's running, no matter what the consequences may be

definitions.text: no matter what the consequences may be

parts.note: a lanky person is tall and thin

indicators.note: letters that are running about are loose and free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gangly Scotsman is out running whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' makes COSTS from the letters of SCOTS (the possessive 's is read as part of the word). A gives itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning regardless of the price or outcome, exactly as the clue's long definition says.

clue.text: Cruel, a French child pinching note

parts.note: UN is the French word for a

indicators.note: pinching means nipping something between, so the word for child holds the note

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A heartless French youngster is caught pinching.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel and unkind are synonyms, both describing behaviour that hurts others.

clue.text: Stinging creature in house on top of nightstand

parts.note: in astrology a house is a sign of the zodiac, and Scorpio is one of them

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here of nightstand

explanation.surface: A creature with a sting is lurking in the bedroom on the bedside table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is the astrological sense: a sign of the zodiac. In a down clue 'on top of' puts the zodiac sign above the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorpion is an arachnid with a venomous sting in its curled tail.

clue.text: Drunk on port? At once!

indicators.note: drunk suggests being thrown about and confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on port demands something immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for immediately, borrowed from Spanish or Italian meaning quick.

clue.text: Wholesale slaughter in field after religious ceremony

indicators.note: after places the field word following the ceremony word

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic ceremony
an acre is a field or piece of land, as in God's acre

explanation.surface: A bloodbath in a field once church is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the indiscriminate killing of many people, which is slaughter on a wholesale scale.

clue.text: Pass on third of motions in legislative assembly

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die

indicators.note: third of selects the third letter of the word motions

explanation.surface: Someone forwards one of three motions in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' reads as forwarding something, but it is the euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal legislative assembly in some countries, such as the Japanese Diet.

clue.text: Huge movie

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means of enormous size
The 1997 James Cameron film about the sinking liner

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means gigantic, and it is also the title of a famous blockbuster film.

clue.text: Film, a new version of Oliver Twist? Oh!

indicators.note: a new version of something remakes it, so the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A film remake of the Dickens novel, met with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new version of' rearranges OLIVER TWIST plus OH. The surface suggests a Dickens adaptation, but the film is the 1967 Sidney Poitier school drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a 1967 British film starring Sidney Poitier as a teacher in London's East End.

clue.text: Studying one planted in newly laid out garden

indicators.note: planted in puts the numeral inside the rearranged letters, like a bulb in soil
a garden newly laid out is rearranged, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone pores over a book while sitting in a freshly landscaped garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly laid out' makes RDEANG from GARDEN; 'planted in' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading means studying, as in reading history at university.

clue.text: Freight train crashed blocking a motorway — a helping hand is required

indicators.note: in this down clue the wrecked train sits right after the A M A, barring the way

parts.note: freight is goods carried in bulk
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: a train that has crashed is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A goods train has crashed across a motorway, and someone needs to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a', beside 'helping hand', belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is just 'helping hand'; 'is required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable, a Good Samaritan is a stranger who helps someone in need, so a helping hand.

clue.text: Private individual lacking energy to keep going

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: one means a single individual
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A private person who runs out of steam still has to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective, but it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for persevering doggedly despite difficulty.

clue.text: Animals turn back, having no right to fight

indicators.note: turn back says the remaining letters run in the opposite direction
having no means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: otters are aquatic mammals

explanation.surface: Creatures retreat because they have no right to brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes R from OTTERS to leave OTTES; 'turn back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or heated argument.

clue.text: One entering road bolted

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the card goes between the two letters

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A runner charges onto the road and dashes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolted and raced both mean ran off at great speed.

clue.text: Angry after golf club medal

indicators.note: after puts the angry word following the club

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
cross means angry

explanation.surface: Someone furious after losing a golf club award.
explanation.walkthrough: In answer order the club comes first; 'after' says the angry word follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Fancy having to quote New Testament in test

indicators.note: in places the quoting and scripture letters within the spoken exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
to name something is to cite or quote it

explanation.surface: Someone fancies quoting scripture in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning decorative.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborate and decorative, the same as ornamental.

clue.text: Hormone treatment for Linus inside home

indicators.note: inside puts the rearranged name between the letters of the word for home

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: a treatment for something works it over, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Linus receives medical care at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' as IN is the sense of being at home, as in 'staying in tonight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar, used to treat diabetes.

clue.text: Liberal getting paid for knowledge

parts.note: earning means getting paid for work

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is paid for what they know.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning means knowledge acquired through study, as in a person of great learning.

clue.text: One carried by old soldier, soldier back in former war zone

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the numeral sits within the veteran

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, an old soldier
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: back says this word is reversed

parts.note: a man is a soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A veteran helps carry a fallen comrade back through an old battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam was the scene of a long war ending in 1975, so it is a former zone of fighting.

clue.text: Travellers — egos vary at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Travellers' self-importance varies when they go on a sea voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Voyagers are people making long journeys, especially by sea, so travellers.

clue.text: Farming economy

definitions.meaning: agriculture and the care of crops and livestock
careful management of resources, an older sense of the word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means agriculture and also thrifty management of money and resources.

clue.text: Tired out going round hospital? That could make one be indecisive

indicators.note: going round puts the rearranged letters on either side of the hospital letter
out suggests something broken or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A worn-out visitor on hospital rounds who can't make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes DITER from TIRED; 'going round' puts it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate, unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Rule amended to include married primate

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters hold the extra one inside
something amended is changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regulation is changed so that it covers married people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' makes LEUR from RULE; 'to include' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in the wild only on Madagascar.

clue.text: Pardon the Parisian, a good sort

parts.note: le is French for the, as a Parisian would say
a toff is an upper-class gentleman, someone of the 'right sort'

explanation.surface: A Parisian forgives a decent chap.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a well-born, well-off gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off is a phrasal verb meaning to excuse or spare from punishment.

clue.text: Mouthpiece for musical instrument

definitions.meaning: a newspaper or publication speaking for a group
a keyboard instrument with pipes, as in a church

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a publication voicing a body's views and the pipe instrument played in churches.

clue.text: Good mimic gets one to stare open-mouthed

parts.note: to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: A skilled impressionist leaves someone staring in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare with the mouth wide open in wonder.

clue.text: Drunk, woolly — and well-organised

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a knit is a knitted woollen garment

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy and in a jumper is still well put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is closely united and well coordinated.

clue.text: Cost of swans being introduced to river

indicators.note: being introduced to means put into, so the swans go inside the river's letters

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: The price of releasing swans onto a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Expense means cost, money spent on something.

clue.text: Hold back female artist during check

indicators.note: during says the female and artist letters come within the checking word

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman painter is told to hold off while being inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to restrain oneself from doing something, a straightforward synonym.
